accepted.title: Nonalternating Chain Walking Polymerization Enables In-Chain Ketone Polyolefin Elastomers
accepted.reason: New catalytic polymerization methodology controlling nonalternating carbonyl insertion and chain walking to synthesize in-chain-ketone polyolefins.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract reports an α-imino-ketone Ni platform, high-MW branched polyethylene products and tunable ketone incorporation; this is directly within polymerization-method scope.
accepted.challengeReason: Although applications are materials-oriented, the central advance is a new polymerization reaction/catalyst platform with structural control, explicitly included by Gallery policy.

accepted.title: Pd-Catalyzed Enantioselective [3+3] Annulation of Vinyldiazos with 2-Iodoanilines Enabled by Sadphos
accepted.reason: General asymmetric annulation methodology furnishing enantioenriched dihydroquinolines from two substrate classes.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract states first Pd-catalyzed asymmetric [3+3] annulation, broad coupling-partner scope, good yields and enantioselectivity.
accepted.challengeReason: Clearly transferable preparative organic synthesis methodology rather than a mechanistic-only study.

accepted.title: Borane-Catalyzed Divergent Hydrogenative and Silylative Reduction of Quinolinium Salts
accepted.reason: Borane-catalyzed divergent chemoselective reduction methodology with solvent-controlled product selectivity.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract reports B(C6F5)3 catalysis affording distinct hydrogenative or silylative products in good-to-high yields.
accepted.challengeReason: Defines a preparative transformation and controllable divergence, squarely within organic-method scope.

accepted.title: Selectfluor-Mediated Radical Cyclization of N-Arylbicyclo[1.1.0]butane-1-carboxamides with Diaryldiselenides
accepted.reason: Radical cascade cyclization methodology constructing selenium-decorated spirocyclobutyl oxindoles.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract reports up to 99% yield across 30 examples, broad functional-group tolerance and gram-scale operation.
accepted.challengeReason: Substrate scope and scalable preparative reaction establish clear general synthetic-method value.

accepted.title: Site-Selective C(sp3)–H Bromination via Radical Relay
accepted.reason: Cobalt-catalyzed site-selective C(sp3)-H bromination methodology via radical relay.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract reports >20:1 benzylic selectivity, broad substrate scope, functional-group tolerance, scale-up and late-stage bromination.
accepted.challengeReason: A broadly useful bond-functionalization method with demonstrated scope and synthetic applicability.

accepted.title: Synthesis of Conjugated Bromoenynoates via Electrophilic Bromination of Enynyl Hydrazones
accepted.reason: Preparative electrophilic bromination methodology giving stereodefined densely functionalized bromoenynoates.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract reports substrate-controlled Z/E divergence, high stereoselectivity, gram-scale reactions and downstream transformations.
accepted.challengeReason: The work develops a transferable synthetic transformation rather than merely characterizing products.

accepted.title: De novo synthesis of threofuranoses via a triple-carbonylation cascade of aldehydes
accepted.reason: De novo carbohydrate synthesis based on a triple-carbonylation cascade is directly preparative organic methodology.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Title and publisher metadata identify a new cascade synthesis of threofuranoses from aldehydes.
accepted.challengeReason: Even without abstract text in the machine record, the title unambiguously describes a new synthetic route/transformation rather than commentary or characterization.

accepted.title: Enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis of multi-helical nanographenes
accepted.reason: Stereoselective synthesis methodology for multi-helical nanographenes.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Publisher title explicitly reports enantio- and diastereoselective synthesis; journal context is synthesis-focused.
accepted.challengeReason: Although the products are functional π-materials, the reported advance is their stereoselective molecular synthesis, which is in scope.

accepted.title: Synthesis of a Fully Functionalized Chasmanine AF-Ring Fragment
accepted.reason: Complex-molecule fragment synthesis with key Piancatelli/[4+2] sequence and a new bench-stable oxidative nitrilation reagent.
accepted.evidenceBasis: Abstract describes an expedient fully functionalized natural-product fragment synthesis and additionally reports a reagent converting aldehydes to nitriles.
accepted.challengeReason: Even though it is a fragment rather than completed total synthesis, it contains a substantive synthetic route and a general reagent transformation, satisfying route/method scope.

rejected.title: Multiobjective Engineering of Fibrin-Selective Thrombolytic Proteases with Enhanced Biocatalytic Efficiency and Inhibition Resistance
rejected.reason: Therapeutic protein/enzyme engineering rather than preparative organic synthesis.
rejected.evidenceBasis: Abstract optimizes protease activity, fibrin selectivity and in-vivo efficacy.
rejected.challengeReason: Biocatalyst engineering is not accompanied by a general organic substrate-to-product synthesis scope.

rejected.title: Alkoxyethyl Acetate Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
rejected.evidenceBasis: Abstract centers on electrolyte solvation and Li/NMC811 cycling.
rejected.challengeReason: Preparation of a solvent molecule is incidental to energy-storage performance, not a general synthesis method.

rejected.title: Deciphering the Multifunctions of Bicarbonate in Acidic CO2 Electrochemical Reduction With Multiscale Simulations
rejected.reason: Mechanistic computational electrochemistry study without preparative organic scope.
rejected.evidenceBasis: DFT, microkinetics and transport modeling analyze CO2RR/HER selectivity.
rejected.challengeReason: No general organic product synthesis or substrate scope is developed.

rejected.evidenceBasis: Abstract centers on Cu-I cluster scintillators and X-ray imaging performance.
